title: Finite-colimit approximation criterion for infinity equivalence
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a common sufficiently large universe. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be quasicategories admitting all finite coherent colimits (diagrams indexed by simplicial sets with finitely many nondegenerate simplices), and let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve these colimits. Suppose $F$ is conservative, meaning an edge of $\mathcal C$ is an equivalence whenever its image is an equivalence. Suppose also that for every $x\in\mathcal C$, every $y\in\mathcal D$, and every edge $\psi:F(x)\to y$, there are $x'\in\mathcal C$, an edge $u:x\to x'$, and an equivalence $e:y\to F(x')$ such that $F(u)$ and $e\psi$ represent the same morphism in $h\mathcal D$. Here $h\mathcal D$ has morphism sets $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(-,-)$. Then $F$ is a functor equivalence, with a coherent quasi-inverse. No hypothesis that $F$ is fully faithful is imposed.

source.place: Dual of Theorem 7.6.10, printed pp. 389-390, with the dual of App 1 and App 2 of Definition 7.6.1, printed pp. 386-387. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result. Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Pass to opposites: put $A=\mathcal C^{op}$, $B=\mathcal D^{op}$ and $G=F^{op}$. Reversing the vertex order of each simplex defines the opposite simplicial set, reverses composition and exchanges coherent colimits with coherent limits; it preserves finiteness of the number of nondegenerate simplices. Thus $A,B$ have finite limits and $G$ preserves them and reflects equivalences. For an edge $\psi:b\to G(a)$, the hypothesis applied to its opposite gives $v:a'\to a$ in $A$ and an equivalence $e:b\to G(a')$ with $[\psi]=[G(v)e]$: take the inverse of the opposite of the equivalence in the hypothesis. An equality in the homotopy category is a path between the corresponding points of the Kan mapping space, so this assertion includes a chosen homotopy after choosing representatives. Call this the right approximation condition. It suffices to give a coherent quasi-inverse for $G$, because taking opposites of that inverse and its two natural equivalences gives one for $F$.

source.place: Definition 7.6.1 and Theorem 7.6.10; explicit passage from left approximation to right approximation

proof.text:
We first establish a reusable intermediate assertion for any $G:A\to B$ with the finite-limit and right approximation hypotheses of step 1: its map on cores is a weak homotopy equivalence. Fix $b\in B$ and let $P_b$ be the homotopy fiber of $G^\simeq:A^\simeq\to B^\simeq$ over $b$. These cores are Kan, and the mapping-path construction makes $P_b$ Kan by [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion]. A map from a finite simplicial set $K$ to $P_b$ gives a diagram $X:K\to A^\simeq$ and a natural equivalence $\tau:GX\to\Delta_K b$. Choose its inverse $\lambda:\Delta_K b\to GX$. Choose a limit cone $\iota:\Delta_K z\to X$ in $A$; its image is a limit cone in $B$. The cone mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that
$$\operatorname{Map}_B(b,Gz)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}(\Delta_K b,GX)$$
is an equivalence. Hence there is $\psi:b\to Gz$ together with a path $G\iota\circ\Delta_K\psi\simeq\lambda$, on the whole coherent diagram, not merely on its vertices. Right approximation gives $v:z'\to z$ and an equivalence $e:b\to Gz'$ with $Gv\circ e\simeq\psi$. Put $\alpha=\iota\circ\Delta_K v:\Delta_K z'\to X$. Then $G\alpha\circ\Delta_K e\simeq\lambda$. Every component of $G\alpha$ is therefore an equivalence, and conservativity makes every component of $\alpha$ an equivalence. The pointwise criterion makes $\alpha$ a natural equivalence. Its simplicial map $K\times\Delta^1\to A$ factors through $A^\simeq$: all edges of $X$, of the constant diagram and of $\alpha$ are equivalences, and the remaining edges are their composites as witnessed by the transformation simplices. Together with $\tau G\alpha\simeq\Delta_K(e^{-1})$, this gives a homotopy in $P_b$ between the given $K$-diagram and the constant diagram at $(z',e^{-1})$. More explicitly the mapping-path fiber is the space of pairs $(X,\tau)$, and a path between such pairs is a path $\alpha$ in the first coordinate with a homotopy from $\tau G\alpha$ to the second path; the displayed coherent homotopy supplies precisely that compatibility. For $K=\varnothing$ the same construction uses a terminal $z$ and produces a vertex of $P_b$.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.7, specialized to equivalences and actual finite limits; expanded contraction of each homotopy fiber

proof.text: The finite-diagram contractions in step 2 make $P_b$ weakly contractible. Here are the required topological details. It is nonempty by the empty-diagram case. For any map $S^r\to|P_b|$, compact finite support [lem-cbc-realization-compact-finite-support] factors it through $|L|$ for a finite simplicial subset $L\subseteq P_b$. Apply step 2 to the inclusion $L\to P_b$. The realization-cylinder homeomorphism of [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] turns its simplicial homotopy into a continuous homotopy of $|L|\to|P_b|$ to a constant. Thus every such sphere map is freely nullhomotopic. For $r=0$ this joins any two points to one point, proving path connectedness. For $r\geq1$, regard a based sphere map as a cube map constant on its boundary, using $[0,1]^r/\partial[0,1]^r\cong S^r$. The basepoint-change formula of [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change] identifies its based homotopy class with transport of the constant class along the track of its basepoint; that transport is zero. Consequently all the based homotopy groups vanish. This proves weak contractibility under the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], including moving basepoints. The homotopy-fiber criterion [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] now shows that $G^\simeq$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Steps 2-3 proved this assertion uniformly for any functor satisfying step 1, without claiming full faithfulness.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.7, finite-test contraction; agent expansion using compact finite support and basepoint change

proof.text:
For $t\in A$ write $S_t=A_{/t}$ for the join slice of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Its $n$-simplices are maps $\Delta^n\star\Delta^0\to A$ with final vertex $t$. It is equivalent over $A$ to the target-fixed arrow category $T_t$ by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence]. We will use its join presentation for finite limits and its arrow presentation for approximation. For a finite $K$ and $q:K\to S_t$, its simplices assemble to $\widehat q:K\star\Delta^0\to A$ with last vertex $t$, as in [lem-coef-join-slice-diagram-isomorphisms]. This shape is finite, including when $K$ is empty. The join cone category of $q$ in $S_t$ is degreewise isomorphic to the join cone category of $\widehat q$ in $A$: an $n$-simplex on either side is a map
$$\Delta^n\star K\star\Delta^0\longrightarrow A$$
restricting to $\widehat q$ on $K\star\Delta^0$. The identification respects all operators by associativity of ordered concatenation. The dual of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison] identifies these join cone categories with the coherent comma cone categories and identifies terminal vertices with limiting cones. Choose a limit of $\widehat q$ in $A$. Its cone gives the corresponding terminal vertex on both sides, hence a limit of $q$ in $S_t$. Applying $G$ to that cone gives a limit of $G\widehat q$ by finite-limit preservation. The same degreewise identification and its naturality therefore show that the induced $G_t:S_t\to B_{/Gt}$ preserves finite limits. For $K=\varnothing$, $\widehat q$ is the single object $t$, so the resulting terminal object in $S_t$ is $1_t$; no assertion that the projection creates empty limits is used.

source.place: Corollary 7.3.29 as used in Theorem 7.6.10; agent explicit finite join-cone calculation

proof.text: The functor $G_t$ also reflects equivalences and has right approximation. Check this in the arrow presentations $T_t,T_{Gt}$, using their natural equivalences with the join slices. The join-slice projections are right fibrations by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Apply the conservativity assertion of [lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift] to their opposites, which are left fibrations because reversing vertices interchanges the horn ranges $0<i\leq n$ and $0\leq i<n$. Hence those projections reflect equivalences. Their arrow presentations are equivalent over the base by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence], so the arrow projections also reflect equivalences. In particular an edge of $T_t$ is an equivalence whenever its source component is, and the same holds over $B$. It follows that $G_t$ is conservative, since $G$ is. For right approximation let $a:c\to t$, $b:d\to Gt$ be objects and let $\psi:b\to Ga$ be an arrow of $T_{Gt}$. Its data are $\psi_0:d\to Gc$ and a homotopy $Ga\,\psi_0\simeq b$. Apply right approximation in $A,B$ to $\psi_0$, obtaining $v:c'\to c$ and an equivalence $e:d\to Gc'$ with $Gv\,e\simeq\psi_0$. Define $a'=av:c'\to t$. The edge $v:a'\to a$ is a morphism over $t$. Equip $e$ with the homotopy $G(a')e=Ga\,Gv\,e\simeq Ga\,\psi_0\simeq b$, obtaining an equivalence $b\to G(a')$ over $Gt$. The homotopy $Gv\,e\simeq\psi_0$, with exactly this chosen composite compatibility, identifies its composite with $G_t(v)$ with the original $\psi$ in the slice homotopy category. This is a statement about the whole slice mapping space: the cone-calculus formula expresses that mapping space as the homotopy fiber of $\operatorname{Map}_B(d,Gc)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(d,Gt)$ over $b$; concatenating the indicated paths gives the path in that fiber. It is not an inference from equality of underlying morphisms alone. Hence right approximation holds in the arrow slices and, via their coherent quasi-inverses over the base, in the join slices. Equivalences transport finite limits by the cone mapping-space criterion and the mapping-space equivalences in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus].

source.place: Proposition 7.6.5 and Remark 7.6.6; explicit compatibility of the approximating triangle in the slice

proof.text:
Steps 4-5 verify every hypothesis of the intermediate assertion of steps 2-3 for $G_t$. Thus both horizontal arrows in the natural square
$$\begin{matrix}S_t^\simeq&\longrightarrow&(B_{/Gt})^\simeq\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ A^\simeq&\xrightarrow{G^\simeq}&B^\simeq\end{matrix}$$
are weak homotopy equivalences: the bottom one by steps 2-3 for $G$, and the top one by the same proved assertion for $G_t$. This use is uniform substitution in an already established assertion, not an application of the theorem being proved.

source.place: Theorem 7.6.10, proof: apply the core argument to the functor and all its slices

proof.text: For clarity, both vertical arrows in step 6 are Kan fibrations, and their ordinary fibers are the required mapping spaces. We check this uniformly for either pair $(E,z)=(A,t)$ or $(E,z)=(B,Gt)$. Put $p:E_{/z}\to E$. This is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], and the dual conservativity assertion of [lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift] makes it conservative, as in step 5. It is also an isofibration in the sense of [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration]. To lift an equivalence $h:p(s)\to a$, choose an inverse $h^{-1}$ and its triangle $h^{-1}h\simeq1_{p(s)}$. First lift $h^{-1}$ with target $s$ using the right $1$-horn lifting property, getting $s'\to s$ over $h^{-1}$. The right $2$-horn consisting of this edge and $1_s$, over the chosen triangle with vertices $p(s),a,p(s)$, fills to an edge $s\to s'$ projecting to the specified edge $h$. Conservativity makes this lift an equivalence. Inner-horn lifting is already part of the right-fibration condition. The core-fibration theorem now makes $p^\simeq$ a Kan fibration. Every simplex in its ordinary fiber over $x$ belongs to the core, since every edge projects to $1_x$ and conservativity makes it an equivalence. Hence its fiber at any $w\in E$ equals the entire fiber of $p$, namely the right-pinched $\operatorname{Map}_E(w,z)$ by the slice theorem. Substituting $(E,z,w)=(A,t,x)$ and $(B,Gt,Gx)$ gives the two claimed fibers. All identifications commute with $G$ because the slice projection and the restriction-to-initial-face formulas do.

source.place: Theorem 7.6.10, proof: mapping spaces as homotopy fibers of core slice projections; explicit isofibration check

proof.text:
For a Kan fibration of Kan complexes, the ordinary pullback over a vertex computes the homotopy pullback: in the replacement description of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] one may use the fibration itself, with its identity weak-equivalence replacement. Apply this to the two vertical arrows of step 6, at $x$ and $Gx$. The map of their homotopy pullbacks is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance]: the maps on total and base spaces are the two horizontal equivalences of step 6, and the remaining map is the identity of the point. Step 7 identifies the induced fiber map with
$$\operatorname{Map}_A(x,t)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_B(Gx,Gt).$$
Thus this actual mapping-space map is an equivalence for all $x,t$; in particular $G$ is fully faithful, including all higher homotopies.

source.place: Theorem 7.6.10, final comparison of the homotopy fibers

proof.text: Let $1_A$ be a terminal object. Its image is terminal because $G$ preserves the empty limit. For any $b\in B$ choose an edge $b\to G1_A$; right approximation supplies an equivalence $b\to G(a')$ for some $a'$. Thus the full essential image of $G$ is all of $B$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to the full faithfulness proved in step 8: its restricted functor is now $G$ itself, so it has a coherent quasi-inverse with both coherent natural equivalences. As explained in step 1, taking opposites gives the required coherent quasi-inverse for $F$.

split_report.summary: Kept the statement and statement dependencies. Gave a nine-step proof: opposite right approximation, an explicit finite-diagram contraction of each core homotopy fiber, compact-support/basepoint verification, finite join-slice limits, approximation in slices with its compatibility homotopy, and comparison of mapping-space fibers. Reused existing nodes only; no new nodes or Mathlib leaves. Avoided the cyclic broad straightening and Yoneda inputs.
split_report.blueprint: Historical master prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint proof paragraph 2, displayed derived coefficient adjunction and inverse-limit calculation; the recorded rectification ancestry uses products of Brown localizations, whose final comparison invokes this finite-colimit criterion. The split supplies that criterion by the dual of Cisinski Theorem 7.6.10 without changing the unit route.

tool_uses.why: The existing generic definitions fix coherent mapping spaces, cores, weak contractibility and functor equivalence used throughout; they are already the statement dependency, not an alternative unit route.

Steps 1, 2 and 5 use Kan mapping spaces, the coherent limit-cone mapping-space criterion, pointwise natural equivalences and the slice mapping-space fiber formula; no coefficient-unit node states this general calculus.

Steps 2 and 3 use the Kan mapping-path replacement and detection of a space equivalence by contractible homotopy fibers; this is a generic space theorem, not a replacement of the coefficient unit route.
